subject: Observability add-ons — annualized savings model, floor clause, and bundle options
messages:

Subject: Observability add-ons — annualized savings model, floor clause, and bundle options

Hi Lena — good to meet you on the call earlier. Per our discussion, attaching a compact pricing matrix that shows three paths for Acme: a seatless ingestion-based plan, a seat-based dashboard bundle, and a hybrid retention + tracing SKU. The spreadsheet breaks out: 30/90/365-day retention tiers, tracing hot path vs archived traces, and an advanced dashboards seat add-on.

Two things I want to call out up front:
- Annualized savings model: the matrix includes a per-unit blended cost assuming 12 months of committed usage (we show per-100k-token and per-gb-ingest equivalents).
- Floor clause (if you choose a committed path): a minimum annual spend that guarantees unit pricing and entitles you to one-time migration credits. We can tune the floor to match your procurement constraints.

Attachment: 20250619-observability-pricing-matrix.xlsx

Next steps: can you confirm whether procurement prefers a true month-to-month pilot or an annual commitment with a 3-month pilot carve-out? I can prepare two SOW sketches depending on that choice.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — annualized savings model, floor clause, and bundle options

Jonas — thanks for the file. A few quick clarifying questions from Acme:

1) Overage protections: if we commit to a floor and exceed the top tier, do overages bill at list or is there a blended cap? We need predictable worst-case in procurement.
2) Floor clause mechanics: can you give an example (numbers) showing how the floor, year-1 usage, and a migration credit interplay? Preferably a before/after annualized cost table.
3) Retention mix: our production traces are heavy on spans; can you show cost delta for 30 vs 90 day tracing hot-path retention for ~2TB monthly?
4) Legal: any special language needed for the floor clause re: termination / true-up?

Also SOC2 evidence and a short security questionnaire were requested by our InfoSec. Can you point me to the SOC2 report and the audit contact?

If you can get answers back by EOD Monday our procurement team can move quickly.

— Lena
Lena Gomez
Senior Product Manager, Observability | Acme Corp
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lena Gomez <lena.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-20T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons — annualized savings model, floor clause, and bundle options

Lena — thanks, good questions. Quick answers and what I attached to help: acme-usage-scenarios-2025.xlsx (two worked examples).

1) Overage protections: for committed annual paths we offer a tiered overage cap structure — overages up to 20% of the committed volume billed at the committed unit price (no uplift). Anything beyond 20% billed at a 10% premium to the committed unit price. For month-to-month pilots we default to list overage pricing but can pre-buy buffer credits that amortize into a blended unit cost.

2) Floor clause mechanics (example): say you commit to $250k ARR (floor). We guarantee the tiered unit price across that spend and provide a $15k one-time migration credit applied to first invoice. If year-1 usage is only $180k, there's a true-up for $70k that is billable unless you opt to downgrade to the month-to-month baseline pricing at contract termination (with a 90-day notice). The example table in acme-usage-scenarios-2025.xlsx shows the per-100k-token annualized cost with and without the credit.

3) Tracing retention: for ~2TB/mo of hot traces, moving from 30 -> 90 days increases storage and query costs roughly 2.4x in our example (indexing and hot-path retention are the drivers). The spreadsheet has a worked scenario with estimated monthly charges and a delta column. We also show a hybrid pattern: 30-day hot retention + 365-day cold archive with compressed trace store — that reduces incremental cost while preserving investigative capability.

4) Legal language: the standard floor clause is a minimum annual commitment with a true-up provision and a termination carve-out (90 days). We typically accept a reasonable drafting in the SOW; Kimberly will flag any nonstandard terms.

Security / SOC2: we have a shared folder with our SOC2 Type II report and an accelerator package for procurement questions. Link: https://drive.redwood.example/security/soc2. Kimberly, can you confirm the pointer and whether we should attach an auditor contact?

I copied Marissa because this is within the deal concession envelope that needs review (migration credit + floor size). I can prepare two SOW drafts (one M/M pilot with pre-bought buffer credits, one 12mo commit with migration credit). Which would procurement prefer?

Thanks,
Jonas

Attachment: acme-usage-scenarios-2025.xlsx
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Internal: approval request — ACME-4721 proposed concessions

Marissa / Kimberly — short note and ask:

Summary: Acme (product + procurement) is evaluating two paths. Recommended commercial that accelerates conversion: 12-month commit at $250k ARR with a $15k one-time migration credit and the tiered overage protection (20% buffer at committed unit price / 10% premium thereafter).

Why: the commit gives Acme predictable unit costs and a simple annualized savings model they can present to finance. The migration credit covers their initial ingestion/simulation costs.

Ask: please confirm we can approve a 20% discount off list (equates to the $250k floor pricing) plus the $15k credit. Also confirm legal is OK with the proposed 90-day termination carve-out on the floor true-up.

If approved I will: 1) send the 12mo SOW with explicitly enumerated retention buckets and the overage cap mechanics, 2) include the DocuSign link and an option for a 3-month pilot addendum.

Thanks,
Jonas

Subject: Final offer and SOW link — ACME-4721 observability add-ons

Lena / procurement team — following internal review we are able to proceed with the committed path:

Offer summary (final):
- 12-month committed path with $250,000 floor (annualized).
- Unit pricing shown in the attached matrix (committed tiers) — blended ~20% off list at the $250k floor.
- One-time migration credit: $15,000 applied to the first invoice.
- Overage protection: first 20% over commitment billed at committed price; >20% billed at committed price +10% premium.
- Retention options explicitly enumerated in SOW: 30/90/365 day buckets plus cold archive path. Advanced dashboards seats billed as optional SKU.

Attached: updated pricing matrix (same workbook updated with Acme scenarios) and SOW sketch. DocuSign SOW link: https://app.docusign.com/Acme/ACM-4721-SOW

If that looks good I will prepare the final SOW and route for signature. We can also include a 3-month pilot addendum that converts to the committed path on signature (migration credit still applies).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the finish line.
